Official Question: Q1: Marketplace Growth & Performance Over Time
Analysis: Monthly longitudinal aggregation of orders, GMV, AOV, mean review score, and late delivery rate
Finding: Rapid order growth (+742% 2017 vs 2016) decoupled from customer satisfaction; quality deteriorated during holiday volume peaks

Analysis: Piecewise linear regression & AIC search across tau in [0.5, 10.0]; logistic regression across 5 delay strata
Finding: Econometric break at tau=0.5d (slope accelerates 3.2x); operational escalation at tau=3.5d (low review rate reaches 72.4%, OR=9.8x)

Analysis: State-to-state flow matrix, Haversine distance calculations, corridor volume and late delivery ranking
Finding: 70.9% seller volume concentrated in SP; 64.0% interstate orders; SP->RJ is largest high-risk trunk (8,065 orders, 20.2% low review rate, 15.3% late)

Analysis: Cross-tabulation of 71 categories, ANOVA interaction model testing Category x Delay on review scores
Finding: Category moderation effect is statistically negligible (partial eta^2 = 0.073%); categories reflect volume exposure, not differential dissatisfaction tolerance

Analysis: Payment method distribution, installment count vs order ticket size, financial reconciliation against GMV
Finding: 73.9% credit card, 19.0% boleto; installment usage scales linearly with ticket value (AOV R$132 for 1x vs R$336 for 10x); no direct satisfaction link

Analysis: 4-level hierarchical attribution, VIF multicollinearity control, 4-factor prioritization matrix, overlap deduplication
Finding: Dissatisfaction driven by structural geography (SP concentration) -> carrier transit (76.9% of duration, OR=2.20) -> delay breach (tau=3.5d) -> survey timing amplifier (OR=12.50x)
